provenance: Rented Vast.ai container, RTX 3070 listing at $0.13/h. Shared host: treat every bandwidth figure as a lower bound with unknown contention.

hardware.gpu: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070 8 GiB (unused: CUDA would not initialise)

bandwidth.note: The 'multi' figure is measured across all 128 logical cores and is meaningless here: the container is entitled to about 18. Oversubscribing collapses bandwidth to a third. Two runs at 128 threads gave 43.8 and 25.2 GB/s, so contention on the shared host is severe. Only the 18-thread figure is used below.

runtime.backend_note: CUDA compiled and linked but refused to initialise at runtime: 'failed to initialize CUDA: unknown error'. PyTorch 2.8.0+cu128 failed identically, so the fault is the host, not llama.cpp. /proc/driver/nvidia/gpus/ listed six GPUs while only /dev/nvidia2 was exposed to the container, and mknod was not permitted.

thread_scaling_tg64.note: Decode gains 6% between 8 and 18 threads, so it is bandwidth-bound rather than compute-bound: the premise the planner rests on, confirmed on a machine unrelated to the one it was built on. Beyond the container's entitlement it collapses, and `nproc` here reports 128.

weight_read_factor.calculation: 26.42 tok/s * 2.147 GB/token = 56.7 GB/s effective, over 74.5 GB/s STREAM add at 18 threads
weight_read_factor.verdict: NOT universal. The constant calibrated on an Intel laptop (1.25x STREAM) does not transfer to this server (0.76x). Contention on a shared host is a plausible confound and this single point does not settle the cause, but it is enough to say the factor is machine-dependent — which is the argument for a hardware registry rather than a constant.

offload_path.note: llama-bench accepted the generated -ot argument without a parse or regex error; the only error on that run was the CUDA init failure shared by all three runs. That rules out a malformed command or a wrong buffer-type name, which was the highest-value failure this exercise was meant to catch. It does NOT confirm the tensors were placed as intended: with no CUDA backend there was nothing to place them on.
offload_path.still_unproven: That the plan beats the CPU baseline on real CUDA hardware, and that it beats --n-cpu-moe.

tool_bugs_found: of probe reports the host's RAM (251.5 GiB) rather than the container's cgroup limit (32.6 GiB).

of probe reports 128 logical cores rather than the ~18 the container is entitled to, and the planner emits no -t recommendation. Accepting llama.cpp's default thread count here would have cost a 4x decode slowdown.
